meta.title: Emendu · From selling devices to a SaaS with its own channel
meta.description: End-to-end product strategy in a B2B IT Management SaaS: redefining the ICP with discovery outside the sales pipeline, optimising the digitisation of the operation and opening a channel through the Sesame HR partnership.

title: From selling devices to a SaaS with its own channel

historia.title: How to scale up the SaaS

bloques.title: Validating who the SaaS was for
paras: Emendu was a **sales-led company with a SaaS on top**, and the brief was not to manage a roadmap: it was to scale up a newly created SaaS within the company.
The first step was validating who it was really for. To do that I joined the sales team in **more than 20 meetings** and interviewed **10 companies that were not in the pipeline**.

That discovery produced a new ICP, and with it the whole 2025 roadmap: evolving the SaaS towards that customer's needs, reorienting LISA and rewriting the product's language for the people who would actually use it.

bloques.title: An in-house engineering team
paras: The next step was iterating on how it was built. I pushed for an **in-house engineering team**, and hiring the **Tech Lead** brought a technical roadmap with order and dates.

bloques.title: When you want to reach further, you build it
paras: With the engineering team focused on the roadmap, I wanted to reach further: what internal stakeholders were asking for, I built myself with **Claude Code**, internal tools for Sales, for Account Managers and for the rest of the company. Not for me: each piece has its own team.

It is also where AI stopped being a lookup tool. Analysing interviews with AI let me review not only the user but **myself as an interviewer**; v0 put working prototypes in customers' hands in the time it used to take to describe them.

bloques.title: From efficiency to channel
paras: With the technical roadmap on the table, **Sesame HR** appeared, and it changed the nature of the project. Until then, optimising the digitisation of the operation was an **efficiency** project, with a known ceiling.
A partnership changes it at the root: the operation stops being only ours and has to work from inside someone else's product too.

caso.title: The Sesame HR partnership
paras: Sesame HR is one of the largest HR software players in Spain, and [the alliance](https://www.economiadigital.es/valencia/empresas/sesame-alia-emendu-suma-gestion-dispositivos-tecnologicos-empresa-plataforma-rrhh.html) brought Emendu's device management into its platform. What follows is how the work was done inside.
**Internal and external discovery, to approach the operation with a new lens.** Interviews with Operations, Sales and Account Managers, and with external sources too.

From there came a **product spec** with features and sub-processes; **flow diagrams as code** with their states and transitions, because a state diagram leaves no room for interpretation where a list of requirements does; and a **navigable HTML prototype, low fidelity and with no UI**, which became the only shared language of four audiences at once: engineering, Operations and Sales, the partner, and product.

items.title: A navigable prototype aligns better than a long specification.
items.text: With an external partner and several teams at once, a low-fidelity HTML did in days what a document would not have done in weeks.

items.title: Optimising the digitisation of a process means designing it from the system.
items.text: It is not about writing code: it is about the operation and the system iterating together, instead of the system merely documenting the operation.

items.title: AI stopped being a lookup tool and became part of the method.
items.text: In interviews, in specs, in prioritisation and in prototypes. That is where my *product builder* stage comes from.
